questions.stem: A balanced, three-phase, delta-connected system has three identical loads of 4 Ω − j3 Ω. The line-to-line voltage is 120 V. Most nearly, the total apparent power in polar form is:
questions.explanation: For a delta load: V_phase = V_line = 120 V. |Z| = √(4²+3²) = 5 Ω. I_phase = 120/5 = 24 A. S_per_phase = V_phase × I_phase* = (120)(24) ∠θ where θ = −arctan(3/4) = −36.87° (capacitive/lagging in Z). S_total = 3 × S_phase = 3 × 120 × 24 = 8640 VA ∠−36.87°. The answer is (C).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Three-Phase Circuits

questions.stem:
Which of these statements concerning transmission lines is FALSE?

![Circuit Diagram](/images/pdf_crops/auto_130_4.png)

choices.A: A standing wave is the sum of the incident and reflected waves.
choices.B: The reflection coefficient is the ratio of the reflected wave voltage to the incident wave voltage.
choices.C: The magnitude of a standing wave is constant at a given position of the transmission line.
choices.D: The standing wave ratio is the ratio of the maximum and minimum current magnitudes of a standing wave.

questions.explanation: A standing wave is formed by the superposition of incident and reflected waves (A is TRUE). The reflection coefficient Γ = V_reflected / V_incident (B is TRUE). The SWR is the ratio of maximum to minimum current (or voltage) magnitudes (D is TRUE). However, the magnitude of a standing wave at a given position is NOT constant — it varies sinusoidally in time (C is FALSE). The amplitude envelope of a standing wave is constant at each spatial position, but the instantaneous magnitude oscillates. The answer is (C).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Transmission Lines

questions.stem:
A step-up transformer is used to connect a large generating plant to the electric grid. Which of the following is TRUE about backup generation in a simple radial distribution system?

![Circuit Diagram](/images/pdf_crops/auto_135_17.png)

choices.A: Backup generation must be connected on the primary side of the supply transformer.
choices.B: Backup generation can only be connected at the utility meter.
choices.C: With proper controls and protection devices, backup generation can be connected on any of the consumer feeders.
choices.D: Backup generation requires a looped or networked distribution topology.

questions.explanation: In a simple radial distribution system, the loads are supplied through a single path from one transformer. While there is no inherent redundancy, with the proper controls and protection devices, backup generation can be connected on any of the consumer feeders — it does not need to be on the primary side. The answer is (C).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Power Distribution

questions.stem: A four-pole induction motor operates on a three-phase, 60 Hz line-to-line supply. The rms voltage is 240 V. The slip is 2%. What is most nearly the operating speed?
questions.explanation: For a 4-pole motor: synchronous speed n_s = 120f/p = (120 × 60)/4 = 1800 rpm. Operating speed n = n_s × (1 − slip) = 1800 × (1 − 0.02) = 1800 × 0.98 = 1764 rpm ≈ 1760 rpm. The answer is (C).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Motors & Generators

questions.stem: A synchronous motor is running at 1200 rpm on a 60 Hz supply voltage. The supply frequency is changed to 50 Hz. Most nearly, the mechanical angular velocity when the motor reaches steady state is:
questions.explanation: For a synchronous motor, n_s is proportional to frequency: n_s2/n_s1 = f₂/f₁, so n_s2 = (50/60) × 1200 = 1000 rpm. Convert to angular velocity: ω = n_s2 × 2π/60 = 1000 × 2π/60 = 104.7 rad/s ≈ 100 rad/s. The answer is (C).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Motors & Generators
